newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar closes sharply off, mixed selling.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar closes sharply off, mixed selling.

text.p: A late bout of mixed selling pressured March CSCE world sugar futures to close at a 10-month low, floor sources said.
The spot month ended down 0.18 cent at 10.17 cents a lb, its lowest since March 8. The rest shed 0.19 to 0.08 cent.
Market sources said local selling emerged when the March contract failed climb toward Monday's high of 10.47 cents.
Aggressive speculative selling came in to pressure the spot month under longterm support between 10.23 and 10.21 cents, and the contract sank to the day's low of 10.10 cents.
Trade buying in the March contract, the March/May spread, and calls in the option ring kept the contract above key psychological support at 10.00 cents, a broker said.

While a slight bounce is expected Wednesday, and the market remains extremely oversold technically, additional selling is likely to pressure prices below 10.00 cents in the near term, market sources said.
Merrill Lynch said in a daily sugar report that some increase in physical offtake is likely at current levels. However, it "should not be sufficient to spark a strong move back up," the report said.
